candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall test the effluent for toxicity in accordance with the provisions in this section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a mandatory WET monitoring obligation; whether this requirement applies to a given facility/outfall/period determines if monitoring was required under Purpose B.
Scopes WET testing to final outfall 001; a different reading of which outfalls are covered would change which discharge points have applicable monitoring obligations.
Sets the effluent dilution threshold used to define acute test failure; a different critical dilution percentage would change whether reported WET results constitute an exceedance.

Specifies the dilution concentrations that must be tested and used to determine NOEC; different interpretation of the required series affects both monitoring design (Purpose B) and compliance determination from test data (Purpose A).

candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines which species and EPA methods govern WET testing; interpretation of required species, method versions, or 'latest version' could change both which monitoring is obligatory (Purpose B) and how results are evaluated for compliance (Purpose A).

candidates.exact_span: SAMPLE TYPE                        Defined in PART I
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defers sample-type requirements to PART I; without resolving that cross-reference, whether grab/composite or other sampling rules apply remains uncertain, affecting monitoring applicability (Purpose B) and how missing or non-comparable results are classified (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: The NOEC (No Observed Lethal Effect Concentration) is herein defined as the greatest effluent dilution at and below which lethality that is statistically different from the control (0% effluent) at the 95% confidence level does not occur.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines how to derive the operative NOEC from test data; alternative readings of the statistical criterion or dilution-bounding rule would change whether a reported WET result is treated as passing or failing.

candidates.exact_span: Acute test failure is defined as a demonstration of a statistically significant lethal effect at test completion to a test species at or below the critical dilution
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the permit's acute WET failure standard tied to critical dilution; different interpretation of 'statistically significant lethal effect' or 'at or below the critical dilution' would change compliance comparisons for reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: This permit may be reopened to require WET limits, chemical specific effluent limits, additional testing, and/or other appropriate actions to address toxicity.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Indicates WET numeric limits are not fixed in this segment and may be imposed later; interpretation affects whether enforceable numeric discharge limits currently exist (Purpose A) versus only narrative failure criteria, and whether additional testing could become obligatory (Purpose B).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall repeat a test, including the control and all effluent dilutions, if the procedures and quality assurance requirements defined in the test methods or in this permit are not satisfied, including the following additional criteria:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Creates a conditional re-testing obligation when QA or method criteria fail; whether a given result is unacceptable and must be repeated affects monitoring-duty status (Purpose B) and whether absent or rejected data should be treated as missing required evidence (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: It is unlawful and a violation of this permit for a permittee or his designated agent, to manipulate test samples in any manner, to delay sample shipment, or to terminate or to cause to terminate a toxicity test.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes that certain handling or termination conduct can invalidate or supplant ordinary test evidence; interpretation affects whether missing or terminated WET data reflects a documented no-data state, a violation context, or unresolved evidence (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: Once initiated, all toxicity tests must be completed unless specific authority has been granted by EPA Region 6 or the State NPDES permitting authority.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Requires completion of initiated tests absent agency authorization; whether an incomplete test was properly excused affects whether monitoring was fully performed (Purpose B) and how incomplete results are classified among missing-evidence states (Purpose C).
